instructions: At least 2 hours ahead, or the day before: set out 4 heatproof cups or ramekins that hold about 3/4 cup each, and check they all fit in a large skillet with a lid.
For the caramel, add 3 tbsp of the sugar and 2 tbsp water to a small saucepan over medium heat. Don't stir. Swirl the pan now and then until the sugar dissolves.
Keep cooking and swirling for 4 to 6 minutes, until it turns a deep amber, like maple syrup. Watch it closely. It goes from amber to burnt quickly.
Turn off the heat and add 1 tbsp hot water. Stand back. It will spatter. Swirl to mix, then pour the caramel into the 4 cups right away, dividing it evenly.

In a medium saucepan, warm the 1 1/2 cups milk, 2 1/2 tbsp of the sugar and the 1/2 tsp vanilla over medium low heat, stirring, until the sugar dissolves and the milk just starts to steam. Don't let it boil.
Meanwhile, in a large bowl, whisk the 3 eggs with the last 2 1/2 tbsp sugar until smooth. Whisk gently so you don't make a lot of foam.
Pour the warm milk into the eggs a little at a time, whisking as you go.
Pour the custard through a fine strainer into a measuring cup or jug, then divide it among the cups over the caramel. Pop any bubbles on top with a toothpick.
Set the cups in the skillet and pour in hot water until it comes about halfway up their sides. Wrap the lid in a clean kitchen towel so drips don't fall on the custard.
Bring the water to a boil over high heat, then turn it down to low, cover with the wrapped lid and simmer gently for 4 minutes.

Turn off the heat and leave the lid on for 15 minutes. No peeking. The custard is done when it wobbles in the middle like jelly but doesn't slosh when you tilt a cup. If it's still runny, cover and keep it on low for 2 to 3 minutes.
Lift the cups out, let them cool to room temperature, then cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour, until cold.
To serve, run a thin knife around the edge of each cup, put a small plate on top and flip it over. Lift the cup off so the caramel runs down the sides. Serve cold.
advance_prep_notes: make at least 2 hours ahead, or the day before, so the puddings chill
method_notes: All three versions pour amber caramel into small cups, cover it with a strained custard of eggs, warm milk, sugar and vanilla, cook it gently and chill it before turning it out. Chopstick Chronicles (the lead) steams the cups in a lidded frying pan of water and lets them finish in the heat with the lid on, which is what this follows; Just One Cookbook's baked version uses a 300°F oven water bath and adds some cream, and its no-bake version sets the custard with gelatin instead of baking. The lead's custard sugar is split between the milk and the eggs here so the amounts match its ingredient list.
